decision.title: try/catch in the evaluator (packet )
decision.summary: TRY_CATCH is one catching task with start, body, handler and finally phases; catch clauses match by name test, bind error details as a map, and finally re-raises a pending error.

item.p: One catching task per TRY_CATCH, phases start, body, handler, finally. The try clause's value is read completely before it counts, so a lazy sequence's error is caught by the try that made it. Catch clauses are tried in order, the first whose name tests match wins (*, EQName, p:*/Q{uri}*, *:local); an error with no code in the record counts as err:FOER0000.

Error details (glossary ): a clause's slot is bound to $err:map, entries keyed by xs:string in table order: "code" (xs:QName, prefix kept only with a namespace), "description", "value", "module", "line-number", "column-number"; none for an empty value. $err:stack-trace and $err:additional are always () in sxml, so they have no entry. Lowering (3.7) reads each $err: variable as map:get($slot, "local-name") and $err:map is the slot. They are copied out of the record before anything else runs ().

Own error record: when the caller passed none, the outermost try points the context's record at one in its task state while it runs and puts NULL back when it ends or unwinds; inner tries use it. Uncaught errors are still reported nowhere. Done inside the part because src/evaluator.c belongs to 2.6 in this wave; the machine may later keep its own record instead, with no visible change.

finally: an error of the try clause that no clause matches, and an error of the catch clause, are caught only to run the finally clause; their details are kept (glossary ) and raised again through the heap when it succeeds (the finally clause may raise and catch errors on the same heap). An error of the finally clause replaces them; a non-empty value is XQTY0153 (type error). Limits, memory and invalid arguments run no catch or finally clause.
XPath 4.0 has no try/catch (checked in the 4.0 draft): nothing for 2.5. XSLT's xsl:try (4.x) can lower to the same kind.
tests/evaluator_machine_test.c no longer expects UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE for TRY_CATCH (list evaluated_kinds, where 3.5 adds the constructors).
